newsitem.title: CHINA: China to tighten checks on imported fruit.
newsitem.headline: China to tighten checks on imported fruit.

text.p: China's Ministry of Agriculture has called for stronger quarantine controls on imported fruit to curb rampant smuggling, state television said on Friday.
Legal fruit imports were worth more than $30 million in the first four months of 1996, up 90 percent from the same period last year, the report said.
But fruit vendors eager for higher profits were buying fruit smuggled into China, increasing the risk of diseased produce being introduced to the country, it said.
Beijing quarantine officials recently carried out spot checks on street vendors, confiscating loads of fruit without quarantine certificates, the report said.
Officials of the bureau contacted by telephone declined to give further details how controls on imported fruit would be tightened.
China in May banned fruit imports from New Zealand's North Island, which was hit by an outbreak of fruitfly.
